source.source: NASA Lunar Communications Relay and Navigation Systems (LCRNS) reference constellation v3.1, Tables 1-2
source.notes: data/relays.py: two-body Kepler from the relay_orbits.csv elements, IAU 2015 Moon rotation to Moon-fixed. Az/el/range by data/geometry.py topocentric() from site04_shackleton_rim at 1739.2 m above the 1737.4 km sphere (PGDA 5 m ground + 2 m antenna), smooth local horizontal, no terrain. Earth: horizons.earth_moon_fixed().

uncertainty.summary: Simulated reference configuration, not an operational constellation: NASA LCRNS reference constellation v3.1 is a government reference design (Intuitive Machines chooses the final one) and is not deployed in this window. Two-body Kepler propagation from the published 2027-03-01 elements (no lunar gravity field or Earth/Sun pull), so positions drift from a real orbit with distance from the epoch; size of the drift unknown. Moon PA frame at J2000 taken as the IAU body frame (~0.03° apart); rotation to Moon-fixed by the IAU 2015 model with TT − UTC fixed at 69.184 s and TDB taken as TT (both negligible here). Epoch 2027-03-01 00:00 read as UTC; if the published epoch is TDB, positions shift 69 s along the orbit. seesEarth: the relay → Earth-centre line misses a smooth 1737.4 km Moon (geometry.sees_earth shortcut: no limb terrain, Earth's centre only). Relay positions are geometric, Earth's is Horizons' apparent one (horizons.track shortcut, ~0.006°).
